title: The Drummer Who Stopped Walking — A Stroke, a Third Nerve Palsy, and a Seizure at Dawn

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
He is 60 years old, a band drummer by trade, and comes in with right-sided weakness that has been present for six days, along with a seizure six days back.

He had been well until seven years ago, when he developed a fever and was incidentally found to have hypertension, which he treated only irregularly from then on. Six years ago he had an episode of giddiness, and doctors told him his blood pressure was uncontrolled and not responding to medication. Around that time he developed weakness affecting both eyes' medial rectus muscles, followed by seizures and a drooping of the right side of his mouth. He was diagnosed with an ischemic stroke involving the posterior cerebral artery, complicated by a third cranial nerve palsy. Since then he has needed support to walk.

Five months ago he had another seizure, this one with tonic movements of all four limbs and five minutes of unconsciousness, without any confusion afterward. Three months ago he stopped being able to walk even with support.

Twenty days ago, weakness began in his right arm and leg. Ten days ago this became a more generalized weakness. Then, six days ago, early in the morning, he had a seizure with tongue-biting, frothing at the mouth, and thirty minutes of unconsciousness, followed by a day of altered behavior — which is what finally brought him to the hospital today.

He has a known history of stroke six years ago and hypertension for seven years, on olmesartan 40 mg, though taken irregularly. He has no known diabetes, tuberculosis, or asthma. He is a non-vegetarian with regular bowel and bladder habits. He has been drinking regularly for 40 years (about 180 ml/day) and smoking three beedis a day for 40 years.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- **General exam:** drowsy, moderately built and nourished; afebrile; pulse 79 bpm; respiratory rate 17/min; blood pressure 150/80 mmHg; no pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, koilonychia, pedal edema, or lymphadenopathy
- **Higher mental function:** drowsy, with slurred speech
- **Cranial nerves:** right eye deviated outward and downward with third nerve palsy; left eye central and normal
- **Motor system:** right-sided hypertonia in both upper and lower limbs (left side normal tone); power 2/5 in the right upper and lower limbs (left side normal)
- **Reflexes:** biceps 3+ on the right versus 2+ on the left, triceps 2+ bilaterally, knee and ankle reflexes absent bilaterally, and bilateral extensor plantar responses
- **Blood counts:** hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL, total leukocyte count 4,800 cells/cumm, lymphocytes 14%
- **Renal function:** blood urea 28 mg/dL, serum creatinine 0.9 mg/dL

sections.heading: How the Story Unfolded on the Ward
sections.content: He was started on antihypertensive therapy (cilnidipine, later increased in dose on day two) along with aspirin-atorvastatin combination therapy and IV vitamin B-complex supplementation, with strict monitoring of fluid intake/output, blood pressure, pulse, and oxygen saturation — management aimed at his recurrent cerebrovascular disease and uncontrolled hypertension on a background of decades of heavy alcohol use and smoking.
